headline: High: shared file and network surfaces make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; no direct pairwise isolation evidence is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can ingest external data and has broad network egress, while oh-my-openagent reads project files and uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks. That creates a plausible path where content from Airbyte-managed data or files is later treated as instructions by the agent. No direct shared-channel proof is provided, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into files that oh-my-openagent reads as prompts or instructions, injection is possible.
IF runtime-injected MCP content is sourced from Airbyte-managed artifacts, the agent may follow attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Separate Airbyte outputs from agent prompt files.
Disable automatic instruction parsing for imported files.
Require provenance tags on any shared artifacts.
Review MCP sources before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlists.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider authentication data, and can call third-party services like PostHog and Exa. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive data can flow from Airbyte into an agent that transmits context externally. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default docs, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or mounted files, business data can be exposed to oh-my-openagent.
IF oh-my-openagent forwards session context to external APIs, copied Airbyte data may leave the environment.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Remove sensitive files from shared directories.
Disable external API calls for sensitive sessions.
Rotate any shared credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API access, while oh-my-openagent has broad network egress, browser/subprocess execution, and multiple-instance support. Their capabilities overlap on mutable external resources and local execution, so concurrent actions can conflict even without explicit shared filesystem writes. Because write-to-same-dir is not documented for Airbyte, this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same external API or dataset, conflicting updates can occur.
IF oh-my-openagent spawns subprocesses while Airbyte is syncing the same resource, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint resources to each agent.
Serialize access to shared APIs.
Pause one agent during critical sync windows.
Use separate credentials per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte produces data pipelines and business data that oh-my-openagent can consume through files, MCPs, or browser-driven workflows. If the agent treats Airbyte outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream support actions or code changes. There is no direct evidence of automated action-taking between them, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Airbyte-generated artifacts are fed into oh-my-openagent without verification, downstream mistakes can propagate.
IF oh-my-openagent uses Airbyte outputs to draft messages or code changes, incorrect data can be acted on.
mitigations: Require human review of Airbyte outputs.
Add validation checks before downstream use.
Mark generated artifacts as untrusted.
Limit agent actions to read-only mode for first pass.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte handles business data, while oh-my-openagent handles session history, provider auth data, and can send data to third-party services such as PostHog and Exa. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty escalates above low because sensitive classes and external transmission are both present.
conditions: IF business data is routed through oh-my-openagent's third-party APIs, retention or residency obligations may be violated.
IF provider auth prompts or session history contain regulated data, compliance controls may be insufficient.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of third-party calls.
Review retention settings for external services.
Separate auth prompts from sensitive datasets.
Document data-flow boundaries for both agents.
requires-engineering: map residency and certification requirements per data class.
